steps: Set the bar in a rack at about mid-chest height. Duck under it and rest the bar across the muscles of your upper back, not on your neck. Grip it with both hands, wider than your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, stand up to lift the bar off the hooks, and take two small steps back. Place your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Take a big breath and tighten your stomach. Keep your chest up and look straight ahead.
Start by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, as if you were sitting down into a chair behind you. Keep your heels flat on the floor.
Lower until your thighs are about level with the floor, or as far as you can go with your back staying flat. Your knees should point in the same direction as your toes.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up, keeping your chest up. Breathe out at the top.
watchFor: Don't let your knees cave inward, and don't let your back round. If either happens, the weight is too heavy or you've gone too low.
Start with just the bar, or with no weight at all. Add weight slowly over weeks.
Set the rack's safety bars just below your bottom position so you can drop the bar onto them if you can't stand up. Never do heavy squats without them or a spotter.
If you get stuck, don't fight it. Lean forward slightly and lower the bar onto the safety bars.

steps: Set the bar in a rack at about upper-chest height. Step up to it and let the bar rest across the front of your shoulders, close to your neck but not pressing on it.
Cross your arms in front, with each hand resting on top of the bar. Lift your elbows so your upper arms are parallel to the floor, which holds the bar in place. Lift it off the hooks and step back.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Keep your chest tall and your elbows high.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower yourself straight down. Keep your heels on the floor.
Lower until your thighs are about level with the floor, keeping your elbows up.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up, keeping your elbows up and your chest tall.
watchFor: If your elbows drop, the bar will roll forward. If you feel it going, drop the weight forward out of the way. Don't try to save it.
Start with a light weight to learn how the bar feels on your shoulders.
Set the rack's safety bars below your bottom position so a failed lift is safe.

steps: Take the bar off a rack at about hip height, or stand it up from the floor. Stand up tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding the bar in front of your thighs with an overhand grip (your palms facing your body), hands just outside your legs.
Soften your knees slightly and keep them at that bend for the whole movement.
Push your hips straight back, as if you're trying to close a door behind you with your buttocks. Let the bar slide down along your legs.
Keep your back flat, your chest lifted, and your head in line with your spine.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch along the back of your thighs, usually around mid-shin. Stop there.
Squeeze your buttocks and push your hips forward to stand back up tall.
watchFor: Keep your back flat. If it starts to round, stop lowering. You've gone as far as your body allows.
The bar stays close to your legs the whole time.
The movement comes from pushing your hips back, not from bending your knees a lot or rounding your back. Start light.

steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the side of a flat, stable bench. Roll a barbell over your legs so it rests across your hips. Wrap a pad or towel around the bar to cushion it.
Plant your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart, knees bent. Hold the bar steady with both hands.
Push through your heels and lift your hips up until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Squeeze your buttocks hard at the top. Keep your chin slightly tucked and your eyes forward.
Lower your hips slowly back down until they nearly touch the floor.
watchFor: Don't arch your lower back at the top. Your ribs should stay pulled down.
Make sure the bench can't slide backward. Set it against a wall.
Start with just the bar and add weight gradually, and keep the bar from rolling.

steps: Take a bar off a rack so it rests across your upper back, on the muscles, not your neck. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a lot of clear space in front of you.
Take a big step forward with one foot, and land so your foot is flat on the floor.
Bend both knees and lower your back knee straight down toward the floor. Stop just before it touches.
Keep your chest up and your front knee pointing the same way as your toes.
Push through your front foot to stand back up and step your back foot up to meet it.
Alternate legs, or finish one side first.
watchFor: Your front knee shouldn't cave inward, and your torso shouldn't lean far forward.
Start with just your body weight, then add the bar when your balance is steady.
Have a clear path and non-slip floor, because a fall with a bar on your back is dangerous. Use a rack with safety bars if you're heavy.

steps: Stand with your feet much wider than your shoulders and your toes pointing outward at about 45 degrees. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, hanging down in front of you.
Keep your chest up and your back straight.
Bend your knees and lower your body straight down, keeping your knees pointing in the same direction as your toes.
Lower until your thighs are about level with the floor.
Push through your whole foot and squeeze your inner thighs and buttocks to stand back up.
watchFor: Don't let your knees fall inward. They should stay over your toes.
Keep your back straight and don't lean forward.
Choose a weight you can hold comfortably, and go only as low as you can while keeping your back flat.

steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the side of a flat, stable bench. Place a dumbbell across your hips and hold it in place with both hands.
Plant your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart, knees bent.
Push through your heels and lift your hips up until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Squeeze your buttocks hard at the top, keeping your chin slightly tucked.
Lower your hips slowly back down.
watchFor: Don't arch your lower back at the top. Keep your ribs pulled down.
Make sure the bench can't slide backward, and put it against a wall if needed.
Pad the dumbbell with a folded towel if it's uncomfortable on your hips.

steps: Stand about two feet in front of a bench, facing away from it. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Reach one foot back and rest the top of that foot on the bench behind you.
Keep your chest up and your front foot flat on the floor, far enough from the bench that your knee will stay behind your toes when you lower.
Bend your front knee and lower your body straight down until your front thigh is about level with the floor.
Push through your front foot to stand back up.
Finish all your reps, then switch legs.
watchFor: Balance is the challenge, so start with no weight until you feel steady.
Don't let your front knee cave inward. Point it the same direction as your toes.
If your back knee or front knee hurts, adjust your foot position, or stop.

steps: Stand facing a sturdy bench or step that's about knee height, with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place one foot flat on the bench, with your whole foot on it.
Push through that foot and stand up straight on the bench, bringing your other foot up to meet it.
Step back down with the other foot first, slowly.
Finish all your reps, then switch legs.
watchFor: Make sure the step is stable and won't slide.
Don't push off the back foot. Let the leg on the step do the work.
Start with a lower step and light weights until your balance is steady.

steps: Stand with your feet a little wider than your shoulders and your toes pointing slightly outward. Hold one dumbbell up close to your chest, cupping one end with both hands.
Keep your elbows pointed down and your chest up.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering yourself straight down like you're sitting into a chair.
Go as low as you can while keeping your back flat and your heels on the floor. Your elbows should fit inside your knees.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up.
watchFor: Don't let your knees cave inward. They should stay pointing the same way as your toes.
Keep your chest up so your back doesn't round.
Lower to a depth that feels comfortable, and go deeper over time.

steps: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. If you have a step, stand with the front half of your feet on it and your heels hanging off the edge.
Keep your legs almost straight and your chest tall.
Push through the balls of your feet and rise as high as you can on your toes.
Pause at the top and squeeze your calves.
Lower slowly until your heels are level with or just below the step.
watchFor: Move slowly and don't bounce.
Hold onto something for balance if you need to.
Don't let your ankles wobble inward or outward. Keep them steady.

steps: Stand on a step with the front half of one foot on it and the heel hanging off. Hold a dumbbell in the hand on the same side as that foot. Rest your other hand on a wall for balance.
Lift your other foot off the floor so all your weight is on one foot.
Push through the ball of your foot and rise as high as you can.
Pause, then lower slowly until your heel is below the step.
Finish all your reps, then switch legs.
watchFor: Hold onto a wall or rail so you can't fall.
Keep your ankle straight and stable, and don't let it wobble.
Start with no weight until your balance is steady.

steps: Sit in the seat and adjust it so that your knees are bent at about a right angle when your feet are on the platform. Put your back and head flat against the pad.
Place your feet flat on the platform, about shoulder-width apart, toes slightly outward.
Push the platform away by straightening your legs. Stop just before your knees lock straight.
Slowly bend your knees and let the platform come back toward you until your knees are at about a right angle.
Push again.
watchFor: Never lock your knees hard at the top. Keep a slight bend.
Don't let your hips lift off the seat or your lower back round at the bottom. If it does, you've gone too deep.
Keep your knees pointing the same way as your toes, and use the safety stops so the weight can't fall on you.

steps: Sit in the seat and adjust it so the backs of your knees are at the edge of the seat. Place your ankles behind the pad. Hold the side handles.
Sit tall with your back flat against the pad.
Straighten your legs to raise the pad until your legs are almost straight.
Squeeze the front of your thighs for a moment at the top.
Lower the pad slowly until your knees are bent at about a right angle.
watchFor: Don't lock your knees hard at the top, and don't swing the weight up.
Use a moderate weight and control both directions. Your knees take the strain here, so start light.
If your knees hurt, stop and lower the weight.

steps: Sit or lie on the machine, depending on its design, and adjust it so the pad rests just above your heels and your knees line up with the machine's pivot point.
Hold the handles and keep your body still.
Bend your knees to pull the pad toward your buttocks as far as you comfortably can.
Squeeze the back of your thighs for a moment.
Slowly let the pad return until your legs are almost straight.
watchFor: Don't lift your hips off the pad or swing your body to move the weight.
Control the weight on the way back. Don't let it snap your legs straight.
If you feel a cramp or sharp pain in the back of your thighs, stop.

steps: Sit in the seat with your back against the pad and place your legs against the pads on the outsides of your knees. Adjust the machine so your legs start close together.
Sit up straight and hold the handles.
Push your legs outward and apart as far as is comfortable, using your outer hips and buttocks.
Pause for a moment, then slowly bring your legs back together.
watchFor: Don't swing or use momentum. Move slowly.
Don't push farther than is comfortable.
Keep your back against the pad.

steps: Sit in the seat with your back against the pad and place your legs against the pads on the insides of your knees. Adjust the machine so your legs start apart, at a comfortable stretch.
Sit up straight and hold the handles.
Squeeze your legs together, using your inner thighs, until the pads meet.
Pause, then slowly let your legs open back up.
watchFor: Set the starting width so it's a mild stretch, not painful. Forcing your legs too far apart can strain your groin.
Move slowly and don't let the weight pull your legs open quickly.
Keep your back against the pad.

steps: Adjust the machine so the pads rest on your shoulders, or on your thighs if it's a seated machine. Put the front half of your feet on the platform, with your heels hanging off.
Stand up straight, or sit up straight if it's the seated version, with your legs almost straight.
Push through the balls of your feet and rise as high as you can on your toes.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until your heels drop below the platform and you feel a stretch in your calves.
watchFor: Move slowly and don't bounce at the bottom.
Don't lock your knees hard.
Keep your back straight, and don't let your ankles wobble.

steps: Set the bar on the Smith machine, which is a barbell attached to vertical rails, at about mid-chest height. Duck under it and rest it across the muscles of your upper back.
Place your feet about shoulder-width apart, and a small step forward of the bar. Twist the bar to unhook it from the rack.
Keep your chest up and your stomach tight.
Bend your knees and push your hips back to lower yourself, like sitting into a chair.
Lower until your thighs are about level with the floor.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up.
watchFor: Know how to lock the bar back onto the hooks. Twist it to hook it at any time if you get stuck.
Because the bar can't move sideways, you have to keep your own balance, so put your feet where your knees and back feel comfortable.
Set the safety stops just below your lowest point.

steps: Set a cable to the lowest position and attach an ankle strap. Fasten the strap around one ankle.
Face the machine and hold on to it for support, with your feet hip-width apart and a slight forward lean.
Keep your standing leg slightly bent and your back flat.
Push your strapped leg straight back and up behind you, squeezing your buttocks.
Pause, then bring your leg slowly back to the start.
watchFor: Don't arch your lower back or lift your leg higher than your hips.
Use a light weight and go slowly. Don't swing the leg.
Keep hold of the machine so you stay steady.

steps: Stand with your feet a little wider than hip-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward. Hold your arms out in front of you for balance.
Keep your chest up and look straight ahead.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering yourself as if you were sitting down into a chair behind you.
Lower until your thighs are about level with the floor, or as far as you can go while keeping your heels on the floor and your back flat.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up.
watchFor: Don't let your knees cave inward. They should stay pointing the same way as your toes.
Keep your heels on the floor and your back flat.
If you can't go very low, that's fine. Go as deep as feels comfortable and work up over time.

steps: Stand up straight with your feet together and plenty of clear space ahead of you. Put your hands on your hips or hold them by your sides.
Take a big step forward with one foot and lower your body straight down by bending both knees.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor, and your front thigh is about level with the floor.
Push through your front foot to stand up, bringing your back leg forward to step into the next lunge.
Keep walking forward, alternating legs.
watchFor: Your front knee should point the same way as your toes and shouldn't cave inward.
Keep your chest up and don't lean far forward.
If you feel unsteady, hold on to a wall or do the lunges in place instead.

steps: Get on your hands and knees on the floor, with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Keep your back flat and your neck long, looking at the floor.
Keeping your knee bent, lift one leg up and back until your thigh is level with your body, pressing your foot toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your buttocks at the top.
Lower slowly. Finish all your reps, then switch legs.
watchFor: Don't arch your lower back or twist your hips to get the leg higher. Keep your hips level.
Move slowly. Don't swing your leg.
Put a folded towel under your knees if the floor is uncomfortable.

steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Rest your arms by your sides, palms down.
Push through your heels and lift your hips up until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Squeeze your buttocks hard at the top.
Lower your hips slowly back to the floor.
watchFor: Don't arch your lower back at the top. Stop when your body is in a straight line.
Push through your heels, not your toes.
Keep your feet flat and your knees pointing forward, not falling inward.

steps: Stand with your back flat against a wall and your feet about a step in front of you, hip-width apart.
Slide your back down the wall until your knees are bent at about a right angle, so your thighs are level with the floor.
Keep your back flat against the wall and your knees directly over your ankles.
Rest your hands on your thighs or hold them out in front of you. Don't push on your legs with your hands.
Hold the position for the target time, breathing steadily. Then slide back up.
watchFor: Keep your knees over your ankles, not out past your toes.
Stop if you feel pain in your knees. A burning feeling in your thighs is normal.
Slide up slowly when you're done, since your legs will be tired.
